title: A small shared-registry conversation with The Cute Syndrome Foundation

sentences.text: At Dravet Syndrome Foundation, we support families affected by SCN1A-related disorders, including Dravet syndrome; The Cute Syndrome Foundation supports SCN8A families.
Both genes help nerve cells send electrical signals through sodium channels.
The atlas infers similar symptom patterns, but its confidence is 0.49, below 0.5—an invitation to explore, not proof that our communities’ needs are identical.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: Simons Searchlight already includes SCN1A families through its registry and online study.
The Registry and Natural History of Epilepsy-Dyskinesia Syndromes lists both SCN1A and SCN8A in its inclusion criteria.
We could compare these resources before proposing anything new.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Please check whether spasmus nutans, EEG spike-wave complexes above 3.5 Hz, and myoclonic absence seizures also occur in SCN8A, rather than treating missing records as absence.
We must read both sides of the contested SCN1A loss-of-function link: some variants reduce protein activity, while others increase it.
The SCN8A link suggesting one working copy is insufficient is atlas-inferred, unverified, and below 0.5 confidence at 0.45.
Before combining information, please check the approval and individual-variant questions below.
Send one exploratory email asking whether the International SCN8A Registry could include SCN1A-related disorders, including Dravet syndrome.
Shared loss-of-function biology motivates this question, but transferability remains a hypothesis.
For discussion of published evidence with a neurologist: do Dravet approvals for fenfluramine, stiripentol, and cannabidiol apply equally to SCN1A-positive and SCN1A-negative patients?
Which individual variants are activating, catalytically impaired, or loss of function—that is, increasing activity, impairing its chemical function, or reducing function?
Dear The Cute Syndrome Foundation team,
I’m writing on behalf of Dravet Syndrome Foundation to explore a small collaboration.
Our communities have a possible biological connection through reduced protein function.
Could the International SCN8A Registry consider including SCN1A-related disorders, including Dravet syndrome?
We would welcome an initial discussion of feasibility and differences before making commitments.
Thank you for considering this conversation.
[Your name], on behalf of Dravet Syndrome Foundation
